title: Holding-time rule
purpose: Add or edit a laboratory holding-time clock for one exact method version, matrix and start/end event pair, for every analyte of the method or for one analyte.
summary: Add or edit a holding-time clock for one method version and matrix, for all its analytes or for one. Only administrators can save; other staff read these values on QC configuration.

tasks.title: Add a holding-time rule
steps: Choose the [[Method]], [[Matrix]], [[Start event]] and [[End event]], and give the rule a [[Name]]. Leave [[Analyte]] on All analytes of the method.
Enter the [[Maximum time]] in hours and, optionally, [[Warn when remaining]].

tasks.title: Give one analyte its own limit
steps: Add a rule with the same [[Method]], [[Matrix]], [[Start event]] and [[End event]] as the method's rule, and choose the [[Analyte]].
Enter that analyte's [[Maximum time]] and select [[Add holding-time rule]]. The other analytes keep the method's rule.

tasks.title: Change a holding-time rule
steps: Open it from QC configuration and change the values.
Explain why in [[Reason for change]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Stop using a holding-time rule without deleting it
steps: Clear [[Is active]], give a reason and select [[Save changes]]. The row and its history stay.

good_to_know: Hours are decimal: 0.25 is 15 minutes, 48 is two days.
An analyte's rule replaces the method's rule with the same start and end events for that analyte only. It can be longer or shorter.
An end exactly at the deadline meets the rule. Later exceeds it.
Changing a rule does not change holding evaluations already recorded on results or reports.
Only one rule can exist for each method, matrix, analyte choice and start and end pair. Edit the existing one.

sections.title: Create, edit and access
paragraphs: Only administrators can open and save this form; other staff read these values on the QC configuration page, where the rows are not links for them. Add creates a new configuration record; Edit prepopulates the existing record and requires a Reason for change. Unknown configuration kinds are unavailable. These are lab policy values, and synthetic seed data is not a validated set.

items.label: Method
items.description: Required exact method/version. The form lists catalog methods, including inactive ones; the rule applies only where this method and matrix are used. A rule on a preparation method applies to results whose prepared portion came from a batch of that method.

items.label: Analyte
items.description: Optional. All analytes of the method (the blank choice) makes a method-wide rule. Choosing an analyte limits the rule to that analyte's tests; it then replaces the method-wide rule with the same start and end events for that analyte, and the other analytes are unaffected. The list holds every catalog analyte by name, but saving is refused unless the method has a test for the analyte in this matrix, or is the required preparation method of such a test, because the rule would otherwise never apply.

items.label: Name
items.description: Required readable clock name, up to 120 characters, shown in evaluations and missing-preparation notices.

items.label: Start event
items.description: Required Collection (composite: end of collection) or Preparation start. The selected event supplies the clock start.

items.label: End event
items.description: Required Preparation start or Analysis start. Preparation-start clocks may end only at Analysis start. Collection may end at either event.

items.label: Maximum time
items.description: Required positive decimal hours (the unit shown beside the box), minimum 0.01, at most two decimal places and nine total digits. The form converts hours to seconds; 0.25 is 15 minutes, 48 is two days, and 672 is 28 days. This is a configured limit, not an observed time.

items.label: Warn when remaining
items.description: Optional positive decimal hours, minimum 0.01, with at most two decimal places and nine total digits. A running clock is At risk when this much or less remains; blank gives no warning window.

items.label: Basis
items.description: Optional method/SOP reference for this clock; document applicable policy rather than relying on synthetic defaults.

items.label: Is active
items.description: Initially checked on Add. Only active rules are used in new entry evaluation and queue deadlines; clearing keeps the row/history but disables its current use.

sections.title: Rules and effects
paragraphs: Only one row may exist for each method/version, matrix, analyte choice (all analytes, or one named analyte) and start/end pair, including inactive rows. Edit the existing row rather than creating a duplicate.

Which rule applies to a test: within each method, for each start/end pair, the active rule naming the test's analyte; otherwise the active method-wide rule. An analyte's rule replaces only the method-wide rule of the same method with the same start and end events, so a method-wide collection-to-preparation rule, or a preparation method's rule, still applies beside an analyte's collection-to-analysis rule. An inactive analyte rule replaces nothing. An analyte added to the method later falls under the method-wide rule until it has a rule of its own.

Deadline equals recorded start plus maximum time. The end event exactly at the deadline meets the clock; later exceeds it. Missing required events or an end before start is Not evaluable. Composite collection uses the recorded collection end, never the start.

New result entry evaluates every active clock that applies to the result's analyte, for the analytical method and any linked preparation method. Queue Hold deadline uses only the shortest applicable active collection-start rule. Preparation-start clocks therefore need actual preparation information and are not fully represented in the queue deadline.

Changing a rule does not rewrite the holding evaluation already captured in an older result revision or issued report. A new entry uses current configuration. Exceeded holding time requires a qualifier marked for holding-time exceedance before submission; missing-event/chronology problems cannot be resolved by a qualifier.

items.label: Add holding-time rule
items.description: Validate and create the configured clock, then return to QC configuration.

sections.title: Save, cancel and history
paragraphs: Validation errors preserve entered form values. A stale record is refused rather than overwriting another person’s edit; input stays visible, but reload and compare current values before saving again. A reload is a new form, so retain any needed unsaved notes before leaving.

items.label: Reason for change
items.description: Optional on creation; required nonblank for every existing-row save. Recorded with actor, time and before/after values.

items.label: Save changes
items.description: For an edit, validate fields and uniqueness, recheck that the record still matches the version opened, and save with its audit event. The Add form’s named submit button creates instead. Success returns to QC configuration.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Return to QC configuration without saving typed changes.

items.label: History
items.description: Existing records show their latest 20 audit events, displayed oldest to newest, with action, actor, time and reason. No history section appears before any events exist.
